anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After satisfies both facts: the single numeric `2` persists course deliver and the same iteration applies the P2 file payload (implementer commit) and the P1 description payload (compare-and-swap, write, readback at 1111…) with no second pick, and `rounds_used` moves to 1 only after the new source commit with `counted: true`/`counted_head`, so the description edit is explicitly round-free; the post-push recheck re-reads the body and rechecks the claim at 2222…, mints P3 instead of silently rewriting, and defers the write to the next iteration. Before kept f2 (readback at 1111…, recheck at 2222…) but fails f1 because it increments `rounds_used` to 1 'before the first mutation', ahead of the description write and independent of any source commit, so the text never shows description work costing nothing — that is the pre-change per-action `fix` model doing exactly what the Change replaces. Keep the After wording: tie the round increment to 'a new source commit in this wave' with the `counted`/`counted_head` checkpoint fields, state once that body-only work and conflict-only syncs have their own accounting, and continue to show the readback plus pushed-head recheck as separate steps so f2 stays visible.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Before refused `deliver` as a non-existent action, so neither payload landed, nothing was read back, and no claim was rechecked; both facts failed there. After maps numeric `2` to the persisted deliver course and runs one iteration that applies the description payload (temp body file, pre-write boundary read, `gh pr edit`, readback of head and body matching the submitted text) and then the file payload (implementer commit, pre-push review, push to 2222...), explicitly stating the body-only repair spends no round and incrementing rounds_used to 1 only after the source commit, which satisfies f1. It then dispatches an affected-only description recheck naming head 2222... with the actual body, finds the no-test sentence contradicted, and mints a new proposal rather than silently rewriting, which satisfies f2. No fact Before kept was lost. If you want to tighten it further, keep the explicit 'read back actual head and body' step immediately after the edit and the explicit 'recheck against the pushed head' step after the push as separate numbered steps as they are now; collapsing them into a single 'reconcile' line would make f2 harder to confirm.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After keeps the round-1 mechanics intact (P1 body write, readback, P2 payload, review, push, then the affected-claim recheck at 2222... that mints P3), so f2 survives. What moved f1 is section 4: instead of rendering the menu with P3's drafted proposal as Before does, After re-enters the next-action check, treats the still-held bare `fix` grant as authority to open a second wave with `selected_ids: [P3]`, and rewrites the body a second time before the human sees anything - a second selection for the description text and a de facto automatic rewrite of the newly contradicted sentence, which the Entry explicitly forbids. Nothing in the worktree-contract change (home:/create:/destroy: keys, ownership match on cleanup) requires this; the regression comes from the next-action loop wording. To keep every fact Before kept while delivering the Change, state that a finding minted by the post-push affected-claim recheck is a new decision boundary: it is rendered at the menu with its own proposal and applied only on the next explicit `fix` pick, never consumed by the retained grant in the same continuation. Keep the worktree sentences (provision at `home:` via `create:` with `pr-<N>`, record `destroy`, ownership match before `worktree.destroy` or forced removal, the `worktree: skipped - outside configured home, left at <path>` line) in the provisioning/cleanup section and leave the wave/round rules untouched.
